web_evidence.title: World Without End — official author-hosted excerpt
web_evidence.note: Sustained opening narration describes Gwenda externally while accessing her sensations, fears, memories, and imagined punishment. No participating narrator frames the scene.

web_evidence.title: World Without End — Encyclopedia.com
web_evidence.note: Literary analysis explicitly identifies third-person omniscient narration and explains that changing character focalization preserves that narrative person.

web_evidence.title: Follett, Ken Writing Styles in World Without End
web_evidence.note: The accessible Point of View section explicitly describes third-person narration focused successively on Merthin, Caris, Gwenda, Ralph, and Godwyn.

web_evidence.title: World Without End Quotes — Goodreads
web_evidence.note: A longer version of q01460 includes an explicit speech attribution, resolving its apparent narratorial I as character dialogue. This is supplementary quote context, not independent whole-book evidence.

search_log: Searched: Ken Follett World Without End excerpt.
Searched: World Without End Ken Follett third person narrative point of view.
Opened and inspected the author-hosted PDF excerpt, Encyclopedia.com literary analysis, and BookRags Point of View section.
Searched quoted passages: World Without End When I'm brave; World Without End I never trust anyone; World Without End My father hated.
Opened the Goodreads work quotes page; its expanded q01460 establishes spoken dialogue.
Searched: Follett I never trust anyone who proclaims. Found a longer Goodreads quotation but no reliable local attribution for q01486.

Searched: World Without End first person narration. Results supplied no credible evidence of sustained first-person sections in Follett's novel; similarly titled works and unrelated narration discussions were disregarded.
person_note: A nonparticipating third-person narrator shifts focalization among characters. Sustained private-consciousness passages in the supplied quotes agree with the authorized opening and explicit whole-book structural analyses. First-person dialogue and Merthin's attributed thought do not constitute person alternation; generic you is likewise nondiagnostic. Some clipped quotations, especially q01486, retain local attribution uncertainty, but there is no credible whole-book conflict. Existing buckets and tense values remain unchanged.
